cohort: 1000 pregnant women attending antenatal checkups in the Obstetrics & Gynecology department of GMC Shahdol, excluding those with multiple pregnancies, chronic medical disorders (diabetes, hypertension, autoimmune disorders, hyperthyroidism, known hypothyroidism), or previous adverse obstetric history with a known cause.
finding: Overt hypothyroidism (TSH >6.2mIU/L) was associated with a higher prevalence of adverse foeto-maternal outcomes (pre-eclampsia, gestational diabetes, IUFD) compared to subclinical hypothyroidism (TSH 3-6.2 mIU/L).
